vopros: What's the best AI receptionist for a small business?

vyzhimka.tekst:
There's no single universal "best" AI receptionist — the right pick depends heavily on your call volume, industry, and budget. It's also worth noting that many "best of" lists online are published by the vendors themselves (e.g., NextPhone's own blog names NextPhone best, Dapta's blog names Dapta best, AIRA's blog names AIRA best), so it's smart to trial a few rather than trust a single ranking. Here's an honest breakdown based on what these comparisons converge on:

## What an AI receptionist actually does
An AI phone receptionist uses conversational artificial intelligence to answer business calls automatically — greeting callers, answering questions, booking appointments, and routing calls 24/7. AI receptionists cost roughly $25 to $160 per month, versus human receptionists averaging about $3,500 per month fully loaded.

## Top picks by scenario

**Best flat-rate / unlimited pricing:** NextPhone is positioned as a flat monthly plan from $199 with unlimited inbound calls, answering in under 2 seconds, resolving 90–95% of calls without escalation, and it's the only flat-rate unlimited model in several comparisons, unlike Dialzara and Goodcall which cap minutes/callers and charge overage fees.

**Best for home services/contractors:** Rosie is aimed squarely at small service businesses — you point it at your website and Google Business Profile, it trains itself on your business, and it's up fastest for contractors and home-services owners. NextPhone also markets itself this way, noting it detects urgency keywords ("pipe burst," "no heat," "roof leak," "no AC") and routes those calls to you immediately.

**Best hybrid AI + human option:** Smith.ai blends live human receptionists with AI, which is a strong fit if you want people in the loop for complex calls, though that human layer raises the price. Pricing runs from $300/month for 30 calls up to $2,100 for 300, plus $8.50–$11.50 per call over plan and per-call fees for booking, recording and payments.

**Best budget/entry-level:** Dialzara ($29/month) and Synthflow AI ($29/month) offer entry-level options for very low call volumes, though Dialzara caps talk time and bills $0.35–$0.48 per minute past it.

**Best no-code, bilingual option:** Dapta handles both voice and text, speaks English and Spanish, and goes live in minutes with no code.

**Best for medical/dental practices:** OmniMD is built entirely for healthcare environments where HIPAA compliance isn't optional and EHR integration is expected, handling things generic tools can't — like insurance eligibility and prescription refills.

**Best for developer/custom workflows:** Retell AI is a developer platform for building low-latency voice agents, while Synthflow is a developer platform for building custom AI voice agents from scratch, suited for businesses with specific workflows off-the-shelf tools can't handle — but if you're a small business owner without technical needs, it's probably not the right fit since setup complexity is real.

**Best if you already use RingCentral:** If you already run a business phone system like RingCentral, check its built-in AI receptionist before adding a separate vendor.

## Bottom line
For a typical small business, the practical shortlist is: **NextPhone or Voksha** (flat-rate, predictable pricing), **Rosie** (fastest setup for home services), **Smith.ai** (if you want human backup for tricky calls), or **Dapta/Goodcall** (quick, no-code setup). Always use the free trial before committing — call the AI yourself 10+ times with realistic scenarios to evaluate voice quality, comprehension, and accuracy. Given how much these vendor blogs conflict, that hands-on test is more reliable than any single ranking.
